title: Explainable hybrid quantum neural networks for analyzing the influence of tweets on stock price prediction
abstract_summary: The paper proposes an explainable hybrid quantum neural network, optimized by a genetic algorithm, that fuses daily average sentiment scores from transformer-based analysis of tweets with historical stock data to predict future closing prices. The model is evaluated on six companies using over 4 million tweets and employs Shapley-based XAI methods to quantify feature contributions, reporting very high predictive performance (R^2 > 99%) and concluding that daily tweet sentiment has little influence on stock closing price in this case study.
methodology_description: The study fuses transformer-based sentiment analysis of social media with a hybrid quantum-classical neural network optimized by a genetic algorithm, and applies Shapley-based XAI to explain feature contributions. Tweets (≈4M) for six companies were preprocessed (remove nulls, punctuation, URLs, hashtags, stop words, single-character tokens; stemming and lemmatization), then each tweet was scored using a GPT‑3 transformer via API. Daily average sentiment (avgScore) was computed and joined (by date) with historical stock data (open, high, low, close, volume, dividends, splits) spanning 2015–2020. The combined dataset was split 70/30 for train/test. Inputs were encoded into a quantum feature map (implemented with Qiskit‑learn / PennyLane), fed through a hybrid quantum neural network (multiple quantum perceptrons / layers with classical neural layers), and trained with a Genetic Algorithm to optimize unitary parameters and hyperparameters. The fidelity (overlap between predicted and target density matrices) acted as the loss; unitary updates preserved unitarity via exponential maps. Training ran for a fixed number of epochs/iterations (reported values) and used GA population operations (selection, rotation-angle updates) until convergence or epoch limit. Evaluation metrics were MSE, RMSE, MAE, and R^2 and comparisons were made against several classical and quantum-inspired baselines (Deep LSTM, Ensemble Deep RVFL, Ensemble Deep ESN, Quantum Decision Tree, Quantum SVM, Quantum Deep ANN, QuantumLeap). Finally Shapley analyses (heatmap, waterfall, cohort, mean-value) were applied to model outputs to quantify per-feature influence. Implementation used Qiskit‑learn and PennyLane for quantum parts and GPT‑3 for sentiment, executed in Google Colab (T4 GPU).
experimental_setup: Implemented and executed on Google Colab (NVIDIA T4 GPU) with CUDA 12.2. Quantum parts were simulated using qiskit-learn and PennyLane (no physical QPU reported). Sentiment analysis used OpenAI GPT-3 via API. Training used a 70/30 train/test split and GA-based hyperparameter tuning.
dataset_used: Two public datasets from Kaggle: (1) Tweets about top companies (2015–2020) — >4 million tweets across six companies (Apple, Amazon, Google, Google-L, Microsoft, Tesla); (2) Historical stock price data (open, high, low, close, volume, dividend, splits) for the same six companies covering 2015–2020. Link provided in paper: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/omermetinn/tweets-about-the-top-companies-from-2015-to-2020.

pipeline_steps: Collect tweets and historical stock prices from Kaggle (2015–2020).
Preprocess tweets: clean text, remove noise, stemming/lemmatization.
Compute sentiment per tweet using GPT-3 transformer via OpenAI API.
Aggregate sentiment: compute average daily sentiment (avgScore) per company.
Fuse avgScore with historical stock dataset on date.
Quantum feature mapping: encode classical features into quantum states using quantum gates (implemented with PennyLane/Qiskit).
Construct hybrid quantum neural network (multiple quantum perceptrons + classical layers); architecture used multiple layers (four layers reported in text; configurable).
Optimize QNN parameters and hyperparameters via Genetic Algorithm (population-based selection, rotation-angle updates of probability amplitudes, mutation probability).
Loss function: fidelity between target and network output density matrices; unitary parameters updated via exponential map to preserve unitarity.
Train for a set number of epochs/iterations (reported epochs) or until convergence.
Evaluate on test set using MSE, RMSE, MAE, R^2; compare to several baseline models.
Apply Shapley (SHAP) analyses (heatmap, waterfall, cohort, mean-value) to explain feature contributions.
experiment_process.notes_on_iterations_and_parameters: Training used GA population updates; iteration continued until epoch ceiling or convergence. Reported/used hyperparameters include step size, number of epochs, GA population size, mutation probability, number of qubits, and number of layers (see experiment_parameters). Exact internal QNN gate sequences, shot counts, and circuit depths are not specified in the paper.

Outputs include predicted vs. actual closing price time series plots and SHAP explainability visualizations indicating feature importances (open/high/low most influential; avgScore had negligible effect).

results_summary: The paper presents an end-to-end pipeline that (1) computes daily average tweet sentiment using a transformer (GPT-3), (2) fuses this sentiment with historical stock features for six companies (2015–2020), (3) trains a hybrid genetic-algorithm-optimized quantum neural network, and (4) applies SHAP-based XAI and statistical tests for interpretation. Empirical results reported in the paper show the proposed hybrid QNN outperforming a variety of classical and quantum-inspired baselines on standard regression metrics and achieving very high R^2 values (>99%) on test sets. Explainability analyses and correlation tests indicate the daily average tweet sentiment contributes little to the closing-price predictions in these datasets. Ablation tests suggest the QNN architecture and hyperparameter tuning materially affect performance, while inclusion of avgScore has only minor effect.

key_ideas: #idea:quantum-advantage — The proposed hybrid quantum neural network (3 qubits, 4 layers) is reported to outperform several classical and quantum-inspired baselines, achieving R^2 > 99% across six company datasets.

#idea:hybrid-approach — The pipeline fuses GPT-3 transformer-based daily average tweet sentiment with historical OHLCV stock data, encodes features via a quantum feature map, and trains a hybrid quantum-classical neural network with a genetic algorithm for parameter/hyperparameter optimization.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — Implementation uses PennyLane/Qiskit simulators on Google Colab with a very small circuit (3 qubits), indicating a NISQ-style, near-term oriented approach (but executed on classical simulators).
#limitation:simulation-only — All quantum experiments were performed via simulation (qiskit-learn / PennyLane) on classical hardware; no experiments on physical QPUs were reported.
#limitation:qubit-count — The study used only 3 qubits, raising questions about scalability to higher-dimensional financial feature spaces and real-world problems.
#limitation:data-encoding — Details on encoding costs (shot counts, circuit depths, explicit gate sequences) are missing, leaving the practicality of encoding large financial datasets unclear.
#limitation:noise — Hardware noise and error-mitigation were not evaluated; simulator results likely omit realistic QPU noise effects, potentially inflating claimed performance.
